fingerprint.algorithm: SHA256 of sorted path + NUL + fileSHA256 + newline records

implemented.canvas: Original Canvas factories and getImageData kernels delegate through explicit admission only in an allocator scope. Per-instance backing setters admit resize first. Backend surfaces/raster owners and successful construction remain retained; finite managed pools destroy dropped/evicted native canvases. Exposure accumulators remain charged, and each finished sample releases its readback.
implemented.sources: Failed construction attempts discard scratch before source rendezvous. Coverage policy headers are separate from actual paint/restore targets, so retries cannot capture a destroyed target. Source, root and independent transfers share their admitted backing stores; retained roots and source canvases cross frame phases explicitly. Local tints/gradient tables retain storage until eviction or disposal.
implemented.actualRelease: The ledger holds admitted owner objects strongly until explicit release and tracks native BYOB backing transfers. Pixel teardown calls native ArrayBuffer.transfer(0), while Canvas teardown zeros original native backing dimensions. No weak-reference/finalizer collection is used for release. Double adoption and foreign transfers fail closed; destruction visits every owner and preserves original null errors.
implemented.body: Exact destination and <=64 KiB BYOB blocks are admitted before a stream fills them. Every transferred receive store is released after copy. Short/long responses, over-quota rejection before reader acquisition and original null stream failure are tested. Responses cancel and readers release on failure.
implemented.scope: This checkpoint covers Canvas renderer storage and cache receive/capture lifetimes. Managed audit resources/oracle pixels are loaded outside this renderer scope. GPU textures/buffers/depth/MSAA, image/font loading, capture/upload, Node queues and full metadata-byte admission remain pending. The production export allocator scope is not enabled yet. These byte counters are declared storage, not physical RSS; per-page peaks are not a simultaneous aggregate peak.
